claim.quote: This is the first event-by-event observation of Cherenkov photons from sub-MeV electrons in a high-yield scintillator detector, and represents a milestone in low-energy particle detector development.

date.note: arXiv v1 date; the CCM talk of July 2026 cites it as Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 171804.

key_value_text.value: Prompt Cherenkov light from sub-MeV electrons isolated with more than 5 sigma confidence using a 22Na source

name: First Event-by-Event Identification of Cherenkov Radiation from Sub-MeV Particles in Liquid Argon

summary.plain: CCM's liquid-argon detector separated the faint, instant Cherenkov light of slow electrons from the much brighter scintillation glow, one event at a time, which lets it tell electron-like signals apart from nuclear recoils.
summary.technical: CCM200 with a 22Na source: prompt time region -6 <= t < 0 ns seen by the uncoated PMTs isolates Cherenkov photons at >5 sigma; basis of a low-background electromagnetic sample and of the first ALP search with a hybrid Cherenkov-scintillation detector at a beam dump.

title: First Event-by-Event Identification of Cherenkov Radiation from Sub-MeV Particles in Liquid Argon
why_it_matters: Event-by-event Cherenkov identification at sub-MeV energies in a high-light-yield scintillator opens direction and particle-type information for low-energy neutrino and dark-sector searches.
